newsitem.title: RUSSIA: World Bank happy with Russia team, ready to lend.
newsitem.headline: World Bank happy with Russia team, ready to lend.

text.p: The World Bank could lend Russia up to $9 billion over three years, Itar-Tass news agency quoted World Bank President James Wolfensohn as saying.

Wolfensohn, speaking to the agency in Washington before a visit to Russia, said he hoped to meet President Boris Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and other ministers. He described the new team of reformers as "a good team".

"We want to support the Russian government in every way we can," he said. "The last time I met Chernomyrdin and Yeltsin... we were firmly convinced that it was essential to develop and strengthen the social programme."
He said the World Bank was ready to invest up to $3 billion a year in loan programmes for Russia, and that this could total $9 billion over three years.
Wolfensohn said he had worked with both Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, Russia's two new first deputy prime ministers, and he had a lot of confidence in them.
He also respected Chernomyrdin and Minister without Portfolio Yevgeny Yasin, who are key players in Russian economic policy-making. "As far as I can see it's a good team," he said.
Wolfensohn, who arrives in Moscow on Thursday and will stay until next Monday, said Russia faced problems during the transitionary period to a market economy.
"I can only express the hope that the current economic leadership succeeds," he said.
